tg_rt_steps_before:
Place the Hub where it has Internet (Wi-Fi, 4G router or 4G modem) and where its MeshCore radio stays within radio range of the team, directly or through repeaters.
Check the Telegram card above: the bot must be connected.
Turn on "Enable private messages".
For each person to reach: type a short name (for example marie), click "Invite a person", then send them the link that appears, by SMS or email. They open it in Telegram and tap Start. Their name then appears under Recipients.
For a Telegram group: type a name (for example team), click "Invite a group", open the link on a phone with Telegram, pick the group and confirm adding the bot.
On each team phone, in the MeshCore app: add the Hub to the contacts. It has the name of its radio. If needed, send an advert from the Hub (Tools → Advert) and from the app.
Once the person appears under Contacts on the Hub, tick them under "Approved contacts".
Try it before leaving: from the MeshCore app, send the Hub the private message @? then @marie test.
tg_rt_guide_field: 2. In the field, from the MeshCore app
tg_rt_steps_field:
Open the private conversation with the Hub. Do not use a channel: everybody would read it.
Write @marie followed by the message, for example: @marie out at 6 pm.
Write @? to get the list of recipients. If it ends with +3, three names did not fit in the message: prefer short names.
The answer arrives in the same conversation, after the name: [marie] ok. For a group: [team/Paul] ok.
A message is 160 bytes at most, @name included: about 150 unaccented characters. An accented letter counts as two. Keep it short: the radio is slow.
tg_rt_steps_tg:
The message comes from the bot, with its author's name.
To answer its author, use Reply on that message. This is the only way in a group.
In a private chat with the bot, a plain message goes to the last person who wrote. If several people write, use Reply to pick the right one. In a chat that also controls the Hub, Reply is required.
The ✍ then 👌 on your answer show how far it went: sent, then received by that person's radio. 💔 means it failed.
Each chat can send 6 messages per minute to the radio.
tg_rt_steps_trouble:
"Unknown recipient": the name is misspelled. The answer lists the possible names.
"Hub offline": the message waits and leaves when Internet is back, unless the Hub restarts meanwhile.
"Not delivered": the person blocked the bot, the bot left the group, or the recipient was removed meanwhile. Send a new invitation.
"Private messages are off": the feature is off on the Hub, or Telegram is off. The message is not sent.
"This invitation is no longer valid": the link was used, is over 24 hours old, the recipient was removed or the Hub restarted. Create a new link.
No answer to @?: the contact is not ticked, or the message does not reach the Hub by radio.
A message from a person who is not ticked arrives in the main Telegram chat, like any other message.
help.release:
A MeshCore radio accepts one connection at a time.

Releasing it disconnects the Hub for the chosen time, so that you can link it to your phone. Meanwhile the Hub relays nothing.
help.wifi:
The Hub's main network, usually your home router.

The Hub uses 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi: it does not see 5 GHz networks. Changing network needs a restart.
help.wifi_alt:
Up to 3 backup networks, by preference.

If the main network is out of reach, the Hub joins the first one of this list it can see, for example a 4G router. It goes back to the main network by itself within 5 minutes of its return, if its signal is strong enough.
help.hostname:
The Hub's name on your network.

With meshcore-hub, the app opens at http://meshcore-hub.local. Letters, digits and hyphens only. If this name does not work on your device, use the IP address.
help.ap_only:
The Hub joins no network and only creates its own Wi-Fi.

For use without Internet: the web app works locally, but Telegram is off.
help.cell:
Lets the Hub reach the Internet with a 4G modem and a SIM card wired to its board.

Meant for boards running Arduino 3, such as the T-Display-S3. The guide in the repository details the wiring.
help.cell_mode:
Backup: 4G only starts once the Wi-Fi has been down for a minute. This uses the least data.

All the time: 4G stays connected, even while the Wi-Fi works. Check your data plan.
help.cell_model: The modem you wired. Choose "Other (standard AT)" for a modem that is not listed and accepts standard AT commands.
help.cell_apn:
Your operator's access point.

Usually leave it empty: the modem uses the one of the SIM. Otherwise enter your operator's APN.
help.cell_pin:
The PIN code of the SIM card, if it has one.

After two refused codes the Hub stops trying, so as not to lock the SIM. The simplest is to remove the PIN with a phone.
help.cell_pins:
The board pins wired to the modem.

TX goes to RXD of the modem, RX to TXD, and the grounds must be connected. PWR turns the modem on: use -1 if it starts by itself.

On the T-Display-S3: TX 43 and RX 44.
help.tg:
Turns the Telegram bridge on.

Without it, the Hub no longer contacts Telegram: no relayed messages, no commands, no private messages.
help.tg_token:
The token identifies your bot.

On Telegram, write to @BotFather, send /newbot, choose a name, then paste the token it gives you here. The Test button checks it.

Keep it secret: it gives control of the bot.
help.tg_chats:
The Telegram chats that control the Hub.

The first one receives all relayed messages. These chats can do everything: write to all contacts, create or delete channels. Only add people you trust.

To link one, click "Link another chat" and send /start to the bot.
help.tg_mode:
Single chat: all messages arrive one after the other, with their author's name.

One topic per conversation: each contact and channel has its thread. In @BotFather, open Bot Settings → Threads Settings and enable Threaded Mode.
help.tg_relay:
Choose what the Hub sends to Telegram: private messages, channels, rooms.

Untick what is too noisy. You can also mute one conversation with /mute.
help.tg_public:
The Public channel is the one the whole network receives: it can be very busy.

When unticked, its messages no longer reach Telegram. They stay readable in the web app, and the other channels keep arriving.

You can still write to it from Telegram with /public.

If channel relaying is unticked, the Public channel is off too.
help.tg_radio: Adds the signal quality (SNR) and the number of hops under each message. Handy to judge the range.
help.tg_skip:
When ticked, messages you write in the web app do not come back in Telegram.

When unticked they appear there too: the whole conversation stays in one place.
help.tg_insecure:
The Hub stops checking that it really talks to Telegram.

Only for short troubleshooting: the token and messages are less protected.
help.rt_on:
Turns on messages of the form @marie text.

When off, a message from an approved contact that starts with @ is not sent, and its author is told: it never goes to the main chat. An answer from Telegram is not sent either. The directory stays saved.
help.rt_dir:
The people and groups reachable from the network.

Click a name to remove it. 16 recipients at most.
help.rt_add:
The name to write after @ on the network: letters, digits, - and _, 20 characters at most. Capitals and accents are ignored. A short name avoids typing mistakes in the field.

This name does not have to be the person's Telegram username: a bot cannot write to someone from their username. It can only write to people who started it: that is what the invitation link is for. It works once, for 24 hours, and restarting the Hub cancels it.

Inviting an existing name again replaces its chat.

Group not offered: in @BotFather, open Bot Settings → Allow Groups.
help.rt_from:
Only these contacts can use the directory, 32 at most. The list protects your bot: a stranger on the network cannot write to your recipients.

Only contacts of the "person" type are listed. If someone is missing, they must send an advert first.
help.rt_keep:
When off, the Hub only records the recipient. A message to Marie shows as "🔒 @marie", and it cannot be sent again.

When on, the text stays readable in the web app by anyone with the Hub's password.

Either way the message goes through the Hub and Telegram in the clear: this is not end-to-end encryption.
help.arduino_ota:
For developers: lets you flash the Hub over the network from PlatformIO or the Arduino IDE, with the Hub's password.

Leave it off if you do not need it.
help.retention:
How many days messages are kept. Removal works by whole months: a message can stay up to one month longer.

0: they stay until space runs out, then the oldest are removed.
help.max_storage: When the board's storage goes past this percentage, the Hub removes the oldest messages.
tg_rt_intro: Approved contacts write "@marie their message" to the Hub from their MeshCore app: only Marie receives it, and her answer only goes back to them.
tg_rt_name_hint: The name your team will write after @ on the network. Pick any name: it does not have to be the person's Telegram username.
tg_rt_link_person: Link to send to this person
tg_rt_link_group: Link to add the bot to the group
tg_rt_link_hint: Valid for 24 hours, once. Restarting the Hub cancels it.
tg_rt_from_hint: Other contacts go through the main Telegram chat, as usual.
tg_rt_keep: Keep the text in the Hub's history
tg_rt_keep_hint: When off, the history only records the recipient: nobody can read the message back on the Hub.

wiz.title: MeshCore Hub setup
wiz.welcome_p: MeshCore Hub replaces your phone: it stays connected to your MeshCore module day and night, keeps every message and relays them to Telegram.
wiz.welcome_1: All your messages (private, channels, rooms) relayed to Telegram, both ways.
wiz.welcome_2: A complete web app, from your PC or your phone.
wiz.welcome_3: Works with every MeshCore module on the market, without a line of code.
wiz.welcome_help: This wizard takes about 5 minutes. Everything can be changed later in Settings. If you get lost, hold the ESP32 BOOT button for 5 seconds to start the wizard again.
wiz.prepare_p: The module must run the "Companion Bluetooth" (or "Companion Wi-Fi") firmware. You can install it from your browser:
wiz.tip_phone: Close the MeshCore app on your phone (or turn its Bluetooth off): the module accepts a single connection.
wiz.tip_pin: Modules with a screen often show a new PIN at each boot: set a fixed PIN in the official app (Settings → Bluetooth PIN).
wiz.tip_range: Keep the module within 5 to 10 metres of the Hub.
wiz.flash_1: Plug the module into a PC running Chrome or Edge.
wiz.flash_2: Open flasher.meshcore.co.uk and pick your model.
wiz.flash_3: Select the "Companion" firmware, Bluetooth (or Wi-Fi) flavour.
wiz.flash_4: Set it up once with the official app (name, radio region), then close the app.
wiz.wifi_p: Pick your home Wi-Fi: it gives the Internet access Telegram needs.
wiz.wifi_need: Pick a network or enable "access point only".
wiz.wifi_help: The ESP32 only works on 2.4 GHz. During the test the MeshCore-Hub access point may change channel: if your phone disconnects, join the MeshCore-Hub network again.
wiz.link_p: Bluetooth works with every module. Wi-Fi TCP is for ESP32 modules flashed with "Companion Wi-Fi".
wiz.link_ble_d: Every module: RAK, Heltec, LilyGO, Seeed…
wiz.link_tcp_d: ESP32 modules with the Companion Wi-Fi firmware (port 5000), or the simulator.
wiz.ble_p: Power the module on next to the Hub, then start the search.
wiz.ble_pin_hint: 123456 by default on modules without a screen. On modules with a screen, copy the PIN shown.
wiz.ble_pick: Pick a module in the list.
wiz.ble_help_2: If the module was paired with a phone, forget it in the phone Bluetooth settings or close the app.
wiz.ble_help_3: PIN rejected? Check it, or set a fixed one in the official app.
wiz.ble_help_4: After the first pairing, reconnections need no PIN.
wiz.err_help.not_found: Module out of range, off, or already connected to a phone.
wiz.err_help.auth_failed: The PIN does not match the module's.
wiz.err_help.no_service: The module does not run a Companion firmware.
wiz.err_help.connect_failed: Try again with the module closer.
wiz.skip_module_q: The Hub is not linked to any module: it can neither receive nor send messages. You can connect it later in Settings → Module connection.
wiz.tcp_p: Enter the module IP address (shown on its screen or in your router) and port.
wiz.tcp_sim: To test without hardware: run python tools/simulator.py on your PC, then use the PC IP.
wiz.tg_p: Receive and send your MeshCore messages from Telegram, anywhere in the world.
wiz.tg_no_internet: The Hub is not on the Internet yet: test the Wi-Fi first (previous step), or skip this step.
wiz.tg_2: Pick a name, then a username ending with bot.
wiz.tg_3: BotFather gives you a token like 123456789:AA…: copy it.
wiz.tg_4: Paste it below and verify it.
wiz.tg_send_start_p: The first chat that sends /start gets locked: nobody else can control the bot.
wiz.tg_no_chat_q: The bot is saved but no Telegram conversation is linked yet: send /start to @{u}. The Hub takes the first conversation that does.
wiz.tg_topics_d: Telegram group with Topics: one MeshCore conversation = one topic (recommended).
wiz.tg_single_d: Everything arrives in one chat, with prefixes. Reply to messages to answer.
wiz.tg_topics_help_t: Setting up a group with topics
wiz.tg_topics_1: Create a Telegram group and enable Topics in its settings.
wiz.tg_topics_2: Add your bot to the group and make it admin ("Manage topics" right).
wiz.tg_topics_3: Send /start in the group to link it.
wiz.sec_p: Pick the admin password: it will be asked to open the web app.
wiz.done_p: Here is the summary. The Hub will now reboot in normal mode.
wiz.qr_hint: Scan to open the app on your phone.
wiz.done_reconnect: After the reboot, connect your phone or PC back to your usual Wi-Fi, then open the address above.
wiz.rebooting_p: Join your Wi-Fi again, then open {u}
wiz.ble_none_heard: The Hub hears {n} Bluetooth device(s), but not your module: it is not advertising. Usually a phone is still connected to it (close the MeshCore app or turn the phone Bluetooth off), its Bluetooth is off in its menu, or it runs a "USB" Companion firmware without Bluetooth.
wiz.ble_deaf: The Hub hears no Bluetooth device at all. Bring the module closer, check the ESP32 antenna and search again.
wiz.ble_failed: The Bluetooth search could not start. Reboot the Hub and try again.
wiz.ble_others: Other Bluetooth devices (if your module has a custom name)
err.path_too_long: Route too long for a trace (more than 16 bytes).
err.contacts_load: Could not load the contact list from the Hub.
err.bad_hostname: Invalid host name: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only (63 characters at most, no hyphen at the start or end).
wiz.wifi_unverified_q: The Hub could not connect to "{s}". If you save it anyway, the Hub may be unreachable after the reboot (its fallback access point only opens after 3 minutes). Save it anyway?
wiz.tg_skip_q: The token you pasted has not been checked: it will not be saved if you skip this step. Skip anyway?
wiz.tg_kept: This bot is already linked to a chat: nothing else to do.
wiz.done_reconnect_ap: After the reboot, the Hub stays in access point mode: connect your phone or PC to the "{s}" Wi-Fi network, then open the address above.
wiz.rebooting_ap_p: Join the "{s}" Wi-Fi network, then open {u}
tg_st_ap_only: Telegram unavailable: the Hub is in access-point-only mode, with no Internet access.
wifi_open_q: No password entered for "{s}". If it is not an open network, type its password before saving, or the Hub will not be able to join it after the restart.
err.bad_chat: "{c}" is not a valid chat_id: only numbers are accepted (e.g. 123456789 or -100123…).
tg_chats_empty_q: With no allowed conversation, the next person who sends /start to the bot will be linked to the Hub and receive your messages. Save anyway?
err.bad_backup: Backup file incomplete or invalid: nothing was imported.
err.bad_host: Enter the module address (name or IP).
cell_intro: Internet access through a 4G modem wired to the Hub (SIMCom A7670 or SIM7600): Telegram keeps working without Wi-Fi. The web app stays reachable only on the Hub's local network.
cell_backup: As a backup, when the Wi-Fi is down (1 min)
cell_apn_hint: Usually leave empty. Otherwise ask your operator for its APN.
cell_pins: ESP32 pins: TX, RX, power key
cell_pins_hint: ESP32 TX to modem RXD, RX to TXD, grounds connected. -1 = no pin (power key if the modem starts by itself). 43 and 44 are for the T-Display-S3 only: on another board, enter the pins you wired.
cell_err.pins: TX/RX pins not set, or not usable on this board. Fix them, then save.
cell_err.no_modem: the modem does not answer (TX/RX swapped? power? power key?). Retrying soon.
cell_err.no_network: no network (SIM inserted? antenna? coverage?). Retrying soon.
cell_err.no_data: data connection refused (check the APN and the plan). Retrying soon.
cell_err.bad_pin: SIM PIN code missing or refused. To avoid locking the SIM, the Hub stops trying: fix the PIN code, then save.
cell_err.sim: SIM locked (PUK code, unlock it in a phone), missing or faulty. The Hub stops trying: fix it, then restart the Hub.
cell_pin_bad: Invalid pin: enter a GPIO number from 0 to 48, or -1 (none).
wifi_alt_hint: When the network above is out of reach, the Hub joins the first one of this list it can see (a 4G router, for example). It moves back to the main network within 5 minutes of its return.
wifi_alt_dup: The same network is listed twice.
